note: He is athletic and far from deconditioned — a working racquet-sports coach who played twelve hours over a weekend and swings a 25 kg kettlebell — so the exclusion criterion is comfortably met. Everything else fails. He is a pickleball coach barely working ('I'm working just a little bit, just doing a few private lessons here and there'), not a business owner or physician; his savings are being consumed by privately funded cancer care, so 'makes good money' does not hold; and health is not the neglected corner of an otherwise good life but the emergency at the centre of it. Most decisively, this is the inverse of good-to-great — he is in the middle of treatment for an aggressive brain tumour and training to survive it, which the stated ICP does not contemplate at all. This is the clearest case in the batch of the observation already recorded against the ICP: it screens on success, income and starting point and has no clinical criterion, so nothing in the stated definition tells a rep to stop here.
